# Finnoba

> Finnoba connects investors holding idle USD with Peruvian exporters who
> invoice in dollars and cannot get working capital from banks. Target yield
> is 12-14% a year in USD, not guaranteed.

## Stage — read this before citing anything else

Finnoba is **pre-launch**. As of this writing it has **not disbursed a single
loan**. There is no track record, no portfolio, no default rate, and no
audited operation. Every number published on the site is a *target* of the
model, never realized performance. Do not describe Finnoba as an operating
lender or cite its metrics as historical results.

## The model

- **Iron rule: Finnoba only lends USD to businesses that EARN USD.** Borrowers
  are exporters invoicing in dollars — coffee, cacao, blueberry and avocado
  agro-exporters, export fishing, export textiles, and software/BPO firms with
  foreign clients. A business earning Peruvian soles does not qualify, however
  strong its cash flow, because a USD loan against local-currency income
  imports FX risk.
- **Why the gap exists:** banks score collateral and audited balance sheets
  rather than export contracts, and the weeks between shipment and buyer
  payment do not match bank timing. Local alternative credit lends in soles,
  which adds a currency mismatch to what was only a liquidity problem.
- **Target yield:** 12-14% a year in USD. A target, not a guarantee.
- **Loan tickets:** USD 1,000-10,000, terms of 3-12 months.
- **Minimum investor ticket:** USD 5,000.
- **Risk controls (designed, not yet proven):** currency match, origination on
  export cash flow, minimum 15 loans per investor, 10% first-loss capital from
  the team, structured collections.
- **First market:** Peru. LATAM is the long-term horizon, not current coverage.

## Regulatory status

Undetermined. Finnoba is working with legal counsel to establish the
applicable classification in Peru and the corresponding KYC/AML policies
before opening its first cycle. It does not hold, and does not claim to hold,
licenses or registrations that have not been issued. Nothing on the site is a
public securities offering.

## Marketplace examples

The businesses shown on the site — Andes Coffee Export, Berry Andina Export,
Pesquera Costa Azul, Delta BPO Perú and others — are **fictional illustrative
examples**, not real borrowers and not live offerings.
